case.name: The payment link for a part-paid 80.00 Retreat place

rule.description:
A reserved booking has a payment link the customer can open without
signing in. It names what they booked, what they have paid and what is
left, and offers to take the rest. It carries no personal details.

What happens after the offer is taken is a payment provider's business
and is not read here.
rule.name: The customer can see what is left

steps.text: a customer owes 80.00 for a Retreat place
they pay a deposit of 30.00
their payment link offers to take the 50.00 that is left
it names the Retreat place, 80.00 ordered and 30.00 paid
it says nothing about who booked

story.description:
Someone can pay part of what they owe now and the rest later. Until they
settle, the organiser must be able to see exactly what is still outstanding.
story.name: A customer pays a deposit and settles the rest later

case.name: A customer opens the booking page of an open bundle

rule.description:
A bundle that hides nothing tells the customer what they are getting
before they buy: the bundle's own name, and each thing inside it.
rule.name: An open bundle names what is inside it

steps.text: a Weekend group holding a Tent at 40.00 and a Breakfast at 10.00
the organiser sells the Weekend as a bundle, with the Tent at 25.00 and the Breakfast left blank
a customer opens the Weekend booking page
the booking page named the Weekend
the booking page named the Tent
the booking page named the Breakfast

story.description:
An organiser can take a group of things they sell and offer the whole group as
one bundle: a tent, a pitch and a breakfast sold together as a weekend. The
bundle sets its own price for each part, so a thing can cost less inside
the bundle than on its own. The organiser can also keep what is inside
private, and sell the bundle purely by its own name.
story.name: An organiser sells several things as one bundle

case.name: The organiser opens the record of someone who has booked before

rule.description:
The counts are shown as numbers they can edit, and the private note is shown
written out. Someone the site has never seen has a record of nothing.
rule.name: The organiser can read what is kept about someone

steps.text: the site has seen Sam book 5 times and get in touch 4 times
the organiser opens Sam's record
the record shows Sam booked 5 times through the site
the record shows 2 bookings the organiser added for Sam
the record shows Sam has visited 9 times
the record shows Sam has been in touch 4 times
the record shows the note about Sam written out

story.description:
The site keeps a little history for each person who deals with it: how many
times they booked, how often they have been in touch, and a private note only
the organiser sees. It is filed under a one-way code made from their email, so
the address itself is never stored. The organiser can read that record and put
it right whenever it is wrong.
story.name: An organiser reads and corrects the record kept about someone

case.name: A customer pays 50.00 for a Workshop place

rule.description:
One sale and one payment, belonging to the same order. No booking fee is
taken unless the organiser has set one up.
rule.name: A paid booking is recorded once, and every page shows the same figure

steps.text: a customer paid 50.00 for a Workshop place
the Workshop earned 50.00 and the customer owes nothing
the booking holds one sale and one payment of 50.00, in one order
no booking fee was taken
every page shows the Workshop earning 50.00

story.description:
When someone pays for a place, the listing earns exactly what they paid, the
customer owes nothing, and every page that shows the figure agrees. The
booking is written down once — one sale and one payment, kept together.
story.name: An organiser sees what a paid booking earned

case.name: The organiser switches back to a saved Stripe test setup

rule.description: Selecting a provider makes it active without removing its saved key.
rule.name: A saved test setup remains available after switching providers

steps.text: a Stripe test key is saved while Square takes payments
the organiser changes the payment provider to Stripe
the payment settings show Stripe selected with its saved key in test mode

story.description:
An organiser can switch between supported payment providers.
A saved provider setup remains available when selected again.
story.name: An organiser chooses a payment provider

case.name: The organiser looks for someone who has not arrived

rule.description:
When a ticket cannot be read, the organiser can pick the person from a list.
That list holds only the people still to arrive, so nobody is let in twice
and a refunded ticket cannot be waved through by hand.
rule.name: Looking someone up by hand only offers people who are not in yet

steps.text: Alice has a ticket for the Ceilidh
the Ceilidh door offers Alice by name

story.description:
On the day, the organiser stands at the door with the listing's scanner open
and reads each person's ticket. The site tells them who is in front of them,
how many places that ticket covers, and whether to let them through. It also
keeps the people already inside off the list, so nobody is counted twice.
story.name: An organiser checks people in at the door

case.name: The organiser creates a private studio floor hold

rule.description: The hold reserves capacity and never becomes a public listing or ticket.
rule.name: A service hold appears to the organiser but not to the customer

steps.text: Ceramics Studio Sessions is available for service work
the organiser creates a two-day Studio floor treatment hold for four places
the admin dashboard shows the Studio floor treatment hold
the public site does not show Studio floor treatment

story.description:
A service event reserves listing capacity without creating a customer ticket.
The organiser can see, duplicate, delete, and cost the hold.
story.name: An organiser holds and costs a service event

case.name: Someone invited as an editor sets a password and logs in

rule.description:
The owner invites them by name and hands over a link. The editor chooses
their own password on that link, and from then on they log in and land on
the listings, which is where their work is.
rule.name: An editor sets up their own account from an invite

steps.text: the owner invites Sam to help with the listings
Sam follows the invite and chooses a password
Sam logs in
Sam is looking at the listings

story.description:
An owner can let somebody help with what the site says without letting them
near the people who have booked. That helper is an editor: they write and
change listings, groups and site pages, and that is the whole of it. They
are never shown a customer's details, what anything earned, or the settings
that run the site — and they hold no key that could open those details even
if they found a way to the page.
story.name: An owner gives someone the run of the listings, and nothing else

case.name: Sam signs up for the set-up shift

rule.description: The confirmation and attendee list show the shift the volunteer chose.
rule.name: A free shift sign-up appears on the organiser's attendee list

steps.text: Oakfield has three volunteer shifts with eight places each
Sam signs up for the set-up shift and asks for step-free access
Sam receives a free booking confirmation for the set-up shift
the organiser sees Sam and the access note on the set-up shift

story.description:
A volunteer can choose one shift and share an access need without paying.
The organiser can see the volunteer and their answer on the chosen shift.
story.name: A volunteer signs up for a free shift
